t: In section 7 of said Act (21 U.S.C. 456) paragraph (a) is hereby amended by deleting the phrase “in or for marketing in a designating major consuming area” and substituting the phrase “otherwise subject to inspection under this Act”; by deleting the phrase “in a designated major consuming area” and substituting the phrase “burdensome effect upon commerce”; and by deleting the phrase “unwholesome or”.

fable.w: This section only makes textual amendments to section 7 of the Act, deleting and substituting phrases about which poultry products are subject to inspection. A reader might suspect the underlying sanitation provision involves regulations or outside parties, but the amending text itself creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with non-federal entities, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to statutory text, changing specific phrases within a definition or standard. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory boards, or hearings. It merely alters the legal criteria for inspection or regulation without involving external participation in the decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: In section 7 of said Act (21 U.S.C. 456) paragraph (a) is hereby amended by deleting the phrase “in or for marketing in a designating major consuming area” and substituting the phrase “otherwise subject to inspection under this Act”; by deleting the phrase “in a designated major consuming area” and substituting the phrase “burdensome effect upon commerce”; and by deleting the phrase “unwholesome or”.

opus.w: This section only amends wording in 21 U.S.C. 456(a) by deleting and substituting phrases. It does not set up any process that brings outside parties into a federal decision. The underlying statute may involve regulations, but nothing in this text grants or requires rulemaking, consultation, hearings, or a right to sue, so the tempting 'Yes' reading isn't supported.
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is that section 7 of the Poultry Products Inspection Act (21 U.S.C. 456) deals with labeling and container standards, which the Secretary may set through regulations. That fails because the SECTION itself only swaps out phrases ("designated major consuming area," "unwholesome or"). It says nothing about rulemaking, comment periods, hearings, advisory bodies, consultation, or a right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any decision.
